task_instance: Complete a partially-filled 3-statement financial model template (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow Statement tabs in an Excel workbook, FY2024A historicals given, FY2025E-FY2029E blank) by filling in formula-driven projections, cross-statement linkages (NI -> CFO -> Cash -> BS Cash, RE roll-forward), balance/cash-tie-out checks, and the standard blue/grey formatting -- the representative core deliverable the skill describes.
blocker_detail: The skill's own CRITICAL PRINCIPLES section specifies exactly two supported delivery paths: (1) live Excel via Office JS (range.formulas, worksheet navigation) inside an Excel Add-in host, or (2) generating a standalone .xlsx via Python/openpyxl, writing formula strings into cells, then running recalc.py before delivery. This office-assistant runtime has neither: no Excel/Office JS host is present, no code execution is permitted (so openpyxl/recalc.py cannot run), and binary file output (.xlsx) is explicitly disallowed -- only text files (markdown, plain text, CSV, JSON, HTML) can be produced. A CSV or HTML fallback cannot substitute for the deliverable: CSV has no multi-tab/cross-sheet live formula linkages or a formula engine to actually evaluate the required checks (Assets=L+E, cash tie-out, NI tie-out, RE roll-forward), and it can't carry the required cell formatting/colors. Hand-computing values and hardcoding them into a text/HTML mock-up is explicitly forbidden by the skill itself ('Formulas over hardcodes (non-negotiable)... If you find yourself computing a value in Python and writing the result to a cell -- STOP') and would misrepresent a static mock-up as a working model. Both of the skill's supported paths require code execution and/or binary file production, neither of which this runtime grants.
evidence: Read the skill document at benchmark/ce_sources_div/anthropics__financial-services-plugins__3-statement-model/SKILL.md and confirmed its 'Environment -- Office JS vs Python' section mandates either live Excel automation or Python/openpyxl + running recalc.py to produce a .xlsx workbook, and its 'Formulas over hardcodes' section forbids writing computed/hardcoded values in place of live formulas. Documented the analysis and attempted fallback approaches (CSV formula-text cells, HTML mock spreadsheet) in task_notes.md, explaining concretely why each fails to satisfy the skill's actual intent (no cross-sheet formula engine, no cell formatting support, and hardcoding violates the skill's non-negotiable rule). No code was executed and no binary file was produced, per the sandbox's safety rules.
